usage: Owner-authored website questions, preserved for offline review; not automatically injected or randomly selected at runtime. Use the client-led rule and one-question limit before adapting any example. This is not the restricted source handout.

groups.title: Starting the Session
groups.purpose: Open the conversation and locate what matters now.
groups.useWhen: The client is arriving with updates, multiple topics or unclear focus.
groups.listenFor: What feels most alive, urgent or meaningful today?
groups.watch: Do not turn the opening into a status-report interview.
qs: What feels most useful to bring into the room today?
What has changed since our last conversation that matters now?
What is asking for your attention most strongly today?
Where would you like to begin?
What feels unfinished from the last time we spoke?
If this conversation served you well, what would we spend our time on?
What are you arriving with today—energy, concern, possibility or something else?
Before we choose a topic, what do you want me to understand about where you are right now?

groups.title: Substance
groups.purpose: Identify the core issue, tension or need beneath the first description.
groups.useWhen: The client has a lot of detail but the central issue is still unclear.
groups.listenFor: What seems to be the real issue under the story?
groups.watch: Do not decide what the 'real problem' is for the client.
qs: What feels most difficult about this situation?
What is the part you keep coming back to?
What is getting in the way right now?
What are you most concerned about here?
What feels most important beneath all these details?
If we removed the noise, what would remain?
What is the tension you are trying to resolve?
What do you most want to understand about what is happening?

groups.title: Clarification
groups.purpose: Make the client's words, distinctions and meaning more precise.
groups.useWhen: A key word, feeling or assumption sounds broad, loaded or ambiguous.
groups.listenFor: What does that word mean specifically for this client?
groups.watch: Avoid replacing the client's language with your own interpretation.
qs: When you say that, what does it mean specifically for you?
What part of this is clear, and what part is still uncertain?
What does that experience feel like from the inside?
What are you distinguishing between here?
What would make this easier to describe accurately?
Which word in what you just said carries the most meaning for you?
What are you assuming I already understand?
If we slowed this down, what exactly is happening?

groups.title: Elaboration
groups.purpose: Help the client develop a thought, feeling or observation without steering it.
groups.useWhen: The client has touched something meaningful but has not fully explored it.
groups.listenFor: What else belongs with what they just said?
groups.watch: Do not use repeated 'what else?' as a mechanical technique.
qs: What else wants to be said about that?
Say a little more about the part that matters most.
What is underneath that first answer?
What are you noticing as you talk about this?
What else are you thinking but not yet saying?
What feeling comes with that?
If you stayed with this for another minute, what might emerge?
What is there more of here than you first thought?

groups.title: Example
groups.purpose: Move from abstraction into a concrete situation the client can examine.
groups.useWhen: The conversation is full of generalisations such as 'always', 'never' or 'people'.
groups.listenFor: What specific moment would make this visible?
groups.watch: Do not use examples to disprove the client; use them to understand.
qs: What is one recent example that captures this?
When did you notice this most clearly?
What did this look like in an actual conversation?
Can you walk me through one moment when this happened?
What would I have seen if I had been there?
Where does this show up most strongly in your day-to-day life?
What is a specific instance that feels representative?
What example would help us understand the pattern without oversimplifying it?

groups.title: History
groups.purpose: Understand prior attempts, patterns and context without getting trapped in the past.
groups.useWhen: Past events or repeated attempts may explain the current pattern.
groups.listenFor: What from the past is useful data for the present?
groups.watch: Avoid turning coaching into a forensic investigation of causes.
qs: What has led to this point?
What have you already tried?
What happened when you tried that?
When have you faced something similar before?
What pattern do you recognise across earlier situations?
What has changed since this first became an issue?
What have previous attempts taught you?
What from the history is important to carry forward—and what can stay in the past?

groups.title: Assessment
groups.purpose: Invite the client to form their own view, judgement or sense-making.
groups.useWhen: The client has information but has not articulated what they make of it.
groups.listenFor: What is the client's own assessment before advice enters?
groups.watch: Do not disguise your evaluation as a question.
qs: What do you make of the situation as you see it now?
What feels most significant to you?
What is your current read of what is happening?
What are you trusting in your own judgement here?
What seems to matter more than you expected?
What feels aligned—and what feels off?
If you had to assess the situation today, what would you say?
What does your own experience tell you that you may be discounting?

groups.title: Evaluation
groups.purpose: Examine fit, importance, trade-offs and meaning against the client's criteria.
groups.useWhen: The client is weighing choices, consequences or alignment.
groups.listenFor: What criteria actually matter to the client?
groups.watch: Avoid imposing what you think should count as success.
qs: What opportunity do you see in this?
What is the real challenge from your perspective?
How well does this fit with what matters to you?
What would make this choice worthwhile?
What are the costs as well as the benefits?
What criteria are you using to judge this?
What does this choice protect, enable or compromise?
Which part of your evaluation feels evidence-based, and which part is assumption?

groups.title: Exploration
groups.purpose: Open territory the client has not yet considered.
groups.useWhen: The conversation is circling familiar explanations or one narrow path.
groups.listenFor: What part of the landscape has not been visited yet?
groups.watch: Exploration is not endless; return to what serves the agreed outcome.
qs: What have you not explored yet?
What other angle deserves attention?
What are you curious about but avoiding?
What possibility have you dismissed too quickly?
What changes if we look at this from a different part of the system?
What question about this situation have you not asked yourself?
What seems outside the frame you are currently using?
If there were one more useful direction to explore, what might it be?

groups.title: For Instance
groups.purpose: Use hypothetical or alternative situations to loosen fixed thinking.
groups.useWhen: The client is locked into one narrative or believes there is only one way.
groups.listenFor: What becomes visible when the situation is varied?
groups.watch: Keep hypotheticals connected to the client's reality rather than fantasy for its own sake.
qs: If you encountered this situation again tomorrow, what might you try differently?
If someone you respect faced this, what might they notice?
If the usual constraint disappeared for a week, what would you experiment with?
If you could rewind one part of this situation, where would you pause?
If you had permission to respond differently, what would you do?
If you were advising your future self, what would you suggest exploring?
If the opposite approach were possible, what could it teach you?
If you could test one alternative without long-term consequences, what would you test?

groups.title: Anticipation
groups.purpose: Help the client imagine possibility, energy and a desired future.
groups.useWhen: The conversation is dominated by risk, limitation or current-state thinking.
groups.listenFor: What future has enough energy to pull the client forward?
groups.watch: Do not use optimism to bypass legitimate fear or constraint.
qs: What becomes possible if this goes better than you currently expect?
What future are you quietly hoping for?
What possibility here gives you the most energy?
Imagine this is working six months from now—what is different?
What would you be excited to tell someone had changed?
If fear became quieter for a moment, what future would you consider?
What are you drawn toward, not only trying to get away from?
What would make this feel worth the effort?

groups.title: Perspective
groups.purpose: Create distance from the current viewpoint and invite a broader frame.
groups.useWhen: The client is fused with one interpretation, time horizon or role.
groups.listenFor: Which perspective could create useful distance?
groups.watch: Reframing should expand choice, not persuade the client to adopt your view.
qs: What might this look like from five years in the future?
What would the person you most respect notice here?
How does this matter in the bigger picture of your life or work?
What changes when you view this as a chapter rather than the whole story?
What would you say about this if you were less emotionally close to it?
How might someone with different priorities see the same situation?
What does this situation look like from the other side of the relationship?
If you zoomed out one level, what becomes visible?

groups.title: Fun as Perspective
groups.purpose: Use lightness, play and creativity to loosen seriousness when appropriate.
groups.useWhen: The conversation is rigid or over-controlled and the client is open to play.
groups.listenFor: Could a lighter frame unlock thinking without minimizing the issue?
groups.watch: Never use humour to dismiss pain, risk or seriousness.
qs: If this could be 20% more enjoyable, what would change?
What would make this experiment feel playful rather than heavy?
What is absurd or unexpectedly funny about the situation?
If you designed the most enjoyable version of this task, what would it include?
What would your more playful self try?
How might curiosity replace some of the pressure here?
If you were teaching someone to bring lightness to this, what would you suggest?
What small element of fun could make the next step easier to begin?

groups.title: Predictions
groups.purpose: Surface expectations and assumptions about what may happen next.
groups.useWhen: The client is acting on an untested forecast or fear.
groups.listenFor: What future prediction is driving today's behaviour?
groups.watch: Treat predictions as hypotheses, not facts.
qs: What do you expect will happen if nothing changes?
What are you predicting other people will do?
How confident are you in that prediction?
What evidence supports your expectation—and what challenges it?
Where do you think this path leads if you continue?
What outcome are you preparing for as though it were certain?
What is the best plausible outcome? What is the difficult plausible outcome?
What prediction would you most like to test rather than assume?

groups.title: Resources
groups.purpose: Reconnect the client with support, knowledge, relationships and existing capability.
groups.useWhen: The client sees the challenge but not what is already available to them.
groups.listenFor: What resources exist inside and around the client?
groups.watch: Resources are broader than people or money; include strengths, information and permission.
qs: What do you already have that could help?
Who could offer perspective, support or access?
What strength have you used successfully in a similar situation?
What information would make the next decision easier?
What resource are you overlooking because it feels too obvious?
Where could you learn what you do not yet know?
What relationship could you activate rather than carry this alone?
What internal resource—courage, patience, curiosity, discipline—would help most now?

groups.title: Options
groups.purpose: Generate multiple ways forward before evaluating or committing.
groups.useWhen: The client has one solution, no solution or a false either/or.
groups.listenFor: Can we create enough choice before deciding?
groups.watch: Do not flood the client with options when they need clarity or emotion to be processed first.
qs: What are three possible ways forward?
What option would you consider if the obvious one were unavailable?
What could you do less of, not only more of?
What is a smaller option than the one you are currently imagining?
What could you combine from two different approaches?
What option protects what matters most while reducing the downside?
What would you try if you did not need to get it perfect first time?
What choice have you not allowed yourself to consider yet?

groups.title: Outcomes
groups.purpose: Clarify the desired result, experience or change the client wants.
groups.useWhen: The conversation needs a destination, success definition or decision criterion.
groups.listenFor: What does the client actually want—not merely want to stop?
groups.watch: Do not force a measurable goal when the useful outcome is insight or acceptance.
qs: What do you want to be different?
What would a meaningful outcome look like for you?
How will you recognise progress?
What do you want to have, know, feel or be able to do?
What is the outcome beneath the first outcome you named?
What would success make possible that is not possible now?
What part of this outcome is within your influence?
If our conversation helped move one thing, what should that be?

groups.title: Planning
groups.purpose: Turn chosen direction into a workable sequence without over-engineering it.
groups.useWhen: The client has decided what they want but needs structure.
groups.listenFor: What is enough planning to create movement?
groups.watch: Do not turn coaching into project management unless that is what the client asks for.
qs: What needs to happen first?
What sequence would make this easier to execute?
What is the smallest useful plan you can commit to?
What needs a decision before action can begin?
What could derail the plan, and how will you account for it?
What would make the plan realistic in your actual week?
What needs to be scheduled rather than merely intended?
What is the next milestone that would tell you the plan is moving?

groups.title: Implementation
groups.purpose: Translate intention into conditions, support and execution details.
groups.useWhen: The client knows the direction but action may fail without practical support.
groups.listenFor: What must be true for this to happen in real life?
groups.watch: Implementation questions should support ownership, not micromanage the client.
qs: What will you actually do next?
When and where will you do it?
What support will make follow-through more likely?
What needs to be prepared before you start?
Who needs to know or be involved?
What will you do when the first obstacle appears?
What can you remove from your environment to make this easier?
What evidence will tell you implementation is working?

groups.title: Taking Action
groups.purpose: Strengthen ownership, commitment and an immediate next move.
groups.useWhen: The client has enough awareness and is ready to choose action.
groups.listenFor: What action is genuinely theirs to choose now?
groups.watch: Do not push action to avoid sitting with unresolved awareness.
qs: What action are you choosing?
What will you do before we speak again?
What is the first move you are willing to make?
When will you begin?
What will you say no to so this action has space?
What commitment feels strong enough to matter and realistic enough to keep?
What will you do if motivation is lower than it is right now?
What would make you leave this conversation and act rather than just agree?

groups.title: Learning
groups.purpose: Extract learning from experience and turn it into future capability.
groups.useWhen: A decision, action or experience has produced useful evidence.
groups.listenFor: What has changed in how the client understands themselves or the situation?
groups.watch: Do not manufacture a lesson from every difficult experience.
qs: What have you learned about yourself through this?
What do you understand now that you did not understand before?
What would you do differently next time?
What assumption changed because of what happened?
What skill or capability are you building here?
What did the experience teach you about what works for you?
What learning do you want to carry into a different situation?
What would make this learning visible in your behaviour?

groups.title: Integration
groups.purpose: Connect insights so they become coherent and usable beyond the session.
groups.useWhen: Several insights have emerged and need to be connected.
groups.listenFor: How do these pieces fit together for the client?
groups.watch: Integration is not the coach summarising the client's meaning for them.
qs: What are you taking away from all of this?
How do the different pieces connect for you now?
What new story are you telling yourself about this?
What do you want to remember when the old pattern returns?
What insight feels most important to integrate into daily life?
How will you remind yourself of what you discovered here?
What changed in your understanding during this conversation?
What will help this insight become practice rather than a good thought?

groups.title: Summary
groups.purpose: Help the client name the essence, progress and unfinished work in their own words.
groups.useWhen: The conversation is closing, transitioning or becoming complex.
groups.listenFor: What does the client want to name as the essence of the work?
groups.watch: Avoid ending with the coach's summary when the client's synthesis is more valuable.
qs: How would you summarize what matters most from this conversation?
What is your clearest conclusion right now?
What shifted for you?
What remains unresolved or worth returning to?
What are the two or three things you want to leave with?
How would you describe the progress you made today?
What are you seeing now that you were not seeing at the start?
If you had to give this conversation a title, what would it be?
